advisories.constraint: Implement robust input validation and output encoding on all user-supplied data (search queries, booking details, personal information) to prevent Cross-Site Scripting (XSS). This includes validating data types, lengths, formats, and character sets. Utilize a Content Security Policy (CSP) to further restrict the sources of executable scripts that the browser is allowed to load, mitigating the impact of potential XSS vulnerabilities. Regularly scan for XSS using automated tools and manual code review.

Ensure all interactive elements (flights, hotels, holiday packages) have sufficient color contrast between text and background as per WCAG 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum). This is vital for users with low vision or color deficiencies.

Implement proper ARIA roles, states, and properties for all dynamic content and interactive widgets (search forms, booking buttons, itineraries) to ensure screen reader compatibility. Focus should be placed on WCAG 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value.

Keyboard accessibility is critical. Verify that all functionality is operable via keyboard alone (WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard). This includes navigation, search, form submission, and interaction with interactive elements like calendars or maps.

Form inputs (search fields, payment information) must have clearly associated labels that are programmatically linked using the `<label>` element. Ensure error messages are descriptive, informative, and programmatically associated with the relevant input field(s) as per WCAG 3.3.1 Error Identification & 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions.

Notifications and alerts should be presented in an accessible manner, using appropriate ARIA live regions to announce updates to screen readers without interrupting user flow (WCAG 4.1.3 Status Notifications). Consider visual alternatives for users who disable notifications.

The application needs to support text resizing up to 200% without loss of content or functionality, as per WCAG 1.4.4 Resize Text. Responsive design should accommodate different screen sizes and orientations.
Ensure any use of time-based media (e.g., for promotional videos) provides alternatives such as captions or transcripts to meet WCAG 1.2.2 Captions (Prerecorded).
